decisions.title: Request↔response correlation uses a blocking single-producer/single-consumer queue
decisions.context: The per-message pump parses each tunnel direction in its own goroutine (parseRequests, parseResponses) and correlates a response to its request through a shared queue. The first implementation was a mutex-guarded slice: parseResponses read the head, then popped the queue, and treated an empty queue as a protocol violation (markOpaque "response without matching request") and aborted the parser. HTTP guarantees the request precedes its response on the wire, but nothing synchronized the two goroutines — copyTee writes to the upstream before teeing to the request parser, and the io.Pipe tee blocks until that parser reads — so under load the response could be parsed and pop the queue before the request goroutine had pushed. Result: a false 'unmatched response', an aborted parser, and every later message in that direction silently dropped. It was intermittent (~1 in 15 under -race) and shipped RED because the prior session verified against cached test results.
decisions.decision: Model the correlation queue as a buffered channel (cap maxPipelinedRequests) with a single producer (parseRequests) and single consumer (parseResponses). popQueue is a blocking receive, so a response that arrives before its request waits for the push instead of racing it. The request goroutine closes the channel at stream EOF (closeRequests, on every exit path including framing loss); a closed, drained queue is the ONLY condition under which an empty queue means a genuinely unmatched response, at which point popQueue returns ok=false and the flow is marked opaque. This makes the request-before-response happens-before a structural property of the channel rather than an unenforced timing assumption.
consequences: Pipelined and keep-alive responses correlate to the correct request under load; no messages dropped on the parser race
A genuine unmatched response is detected at request-EOF instead of immediately — strictly fewer false positives, and the relay keeps forwarding bytes meanwhile
No deadlock: the consumer only ever waits on the producer, which closes the channel on every exit path, so a response waiting on a request that never arrives is always released
Detection of a real protocol violation is deferred to connection close rather than mid-stream — an accepted latency tradeoff for correctness

Guarded by deterministic unit tests on the queue contract (pop-before-push blocks then correlates; closed empty queue returns unmatched), since the race itself is not reproducible under the -count=1 CI run

decisions.title: Liveness is derived once in interpret and feeds both scoring and display
decisions.context: Run-state was display-only (mark.Classify, 2-state ▸/†) and computed after interpret. A dead persistence remnant (disabled .bak + missing target, the com.ironclad.agent case) therefore scored the same as a live, loaded agent, and the mark layer re-derived a run-state the scorer never saw — a DRY split that could drift.
decisions.decision: interpret.livenessState derives a 3-state run-state (active ▸ / armed ◐ / dormant †) once, against the live-process set passed into Assess, and stores it on Assessment.Liveness. recommend() caps a dormant subject at Monitor (it cannot execute) unless a tripwire fires; active/armed keep the score-based recommendation (down-weight the dead, never up-weight the live). mark.Classify now only maps that single value to a glyph and adds the socket mark. This reverses the earlier 'liveness never influences scoring' invariant, but only ever to LOWER urgency, so it cannot manufacture a false escalation. Assess itself stays I/O-free — the caller collects running paths — so verdicts remain reproducible from (findings, running).
consequences: A dead remnant no longer reads as urgently as a live agent
Scored and displayed run-state are the same value — cannot disagree
armed ◐ distinguishes loaded-not-running from dormant in the UI
A --from snapshot carries its scan-time liveness, not a re-derivation against a different machine
Liveness can only reduce a recommendation, never escalate — no new false-positive surface

decisions.title: The scoring engine is a pure function
decisions.context: Scoring is the risk center; it must be testable and free of side effects so weights can be tuned with confidence.
decisions.decision: internal/score is a pure Score([]Evidence) []Finding with no I/O — collectors do all I/O at the edge, so the entire brain is unit-tested from fixtures.
consequences: Zero-risk to run
Fully fixture-testable
Weights live only in weights.go (no magic numbers)

decisions.title: Quarantine moves, never deletes
decisions.context: A false positive on an irreversible delete could destroy data or brick the Mac.
decisions.decision: Quarantine only disables and MOVES artifacts into a timestamped mirror with a manifest; restore round-trips byte-identically and refuses to clobber. Permanent deletion is a separate human step outside the tool.
consequences: Every action is reversible
Manifest is the undo and the RCA trail
Partial failures remain recoverable

decisions.title: Verdicts are rule-based, not model-generated
decisions.context: The tool recommends quarantining people's software; its recommendations must be reproducible and auditable.
decisions.decision: internal/interpret derives verdict/category/recommendation from deterministic rules over the evidence — no LLM in the decision path — so a reviewer (or the ABORT gate) can confirm or refute every label.
consequences: Reproducible verdicts
Auditable by a release gate
Synthesis lives in the core so CLI/TUI share it

decisions.title: Process evidence is keyed by PID, not argv[0]
decisions.context: argv[0] is attacker-controlled; using it as identity let a malicious listener alias onto an allowlisted app and be suppressed.
decisions.decision: Process evidence uses a PID-only Subject; argv[0] is kept only as a display fact. Safe real-path resolution is deferred (ticket T-4).
consequences: A listener cannot hide by spoofing a trusted path
Process/binary correlation is weaker until T-4

decisions.title: Inspection tells the truth about coverage and shows the wire bytes
decisions.context: An inspector that overstates ('encrypted') or hides ('nothing to view') undermines the tool's credibility. A cleartext binary payload once read as 'ENCRYPTED (TLS)' because its bytes looked like ciphertext.
decisions.decision: 'Encrypted (TLS)' requires positive evidence (a ClientHello SNI, a TLS record, or a well-known TLS port), never merely non-printable bytes. Captured bytes are always shown — readable text as text, cleartext-binary as a hexdump — while TLS ciphertext is withheld as noise. This revises the earlier §6 'never render encrypted' rule, which over-hid.
consequences: Verdicts match reality (no false TLS labels)
The actual outbound payload is inspectable, even when binary
Secrets in readable text still masked until reveal

decisions.title: Phase 2 intercepts TLS via a consented CONNECT proxy (pf rdr disproved by smoke test)
decisions.context: Passive egress observation (Phase 1) names destinations but TLS payloads stay opaque. Phase 2 was approved with a TRANSPARENT pf rdr redirect of :443. A root smoke test disproved that mechanism: pf translates only INBOUND packets, so a maximally permissive rule (rdr pass inet proto tcp from any to any port = 443) logged 27828 Evaluations and 0 Packets against the machine's own outbound curl. It cannot fail to match an EVALUATED v4 SYN to 443, so locally-originated packets are never evaluated at all. Linux has iptables OUTPUT REDIRECT and FreeBSD has divert-to; macOS pf has neither, so no rule tuning could fix it.
decisions.decision: Intercept via an HTTP CONNECT proxy registered as the macOS system secure-web proxy (networksetup), not a transparent redirect. The client NAMES its destination in CONNECT, which is authoritative (better than the inferred lookup it replaces) and yields the real hostname without SNI — so pf_darwin.go, pfioc_natlook, DIOCNATLOOK and the anchor machinery were DELETED rather than repaired. Everything downstream (CA, pump, sinks, masking, teardown) was unchanged and is verified. Arming requires per-launch consent and always reverts. Accepted tradeoff: this is COOPERATIVE — apps honoring the system proxy are seen, evasive software is not; a NetworkExtension transparent proxy is approved as a LATER phase to close that gap. Redact/block stays Phase 3.
consequences: The user sees decrypted plaintext of their own outbound TLS (masked) — verified live: Proton Mail Sentry telemetry, iTunes commerce endpoints
Cert-pinned apps reject the leaf and are shown honestly as 'pinned' (bypassed, not decrypted), never faked
Evasive software that ignores the system proxy is NOT covered — an honest, documented gap, not a silent one
The whole pf/ioctl layer is gone: less code, no root-only struct layout to keep in sync with xnu
Interception cannot silently persist: teardown reverts the system proxy + trust on every exit path
A NetworkExtension transparent proxy would require an app bundle + entitlement — a distribution change, scoped as a later phase
